terms.gloss: grow, cultivate (plants, a field, a garden)
terms.comment: Of tending crops through the year: vītem, pōma, hortum colere. Putting them in the ground is serere.

evidence: Caecilius in Cic. Sen. 24: serit arborēs
Varr. RR 1.35.1: serere līlium et crocum

terms.gloss: grow a beard (one’s hair), let it grow
evidence: Liv. 6.16.4: multōs mortālēs capillum ac barbam prōmīsisse
terms.comment: In Livy men let hair and beard grow in mourning; prōmissus is long, of hair or a beard (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: praise big farms; farm a small one

phrases.latin: serit arborēs, quae alterī saeclō prōsint
phrases.english: he plants trees to be of use to the next generation

phrases.latin: spēs ūnica imperiī populī Rōmānī L. Quīnctius trāns Tiberim … quattuor jūgerum colēbat agrum
phrases.english: the one hope of Rome’s empire, Lucius Quinctius, farmed a plot of four acres across the Tiber

sources: Lewis & Short: colo · Lewis & Short: sero · Lewis & Short: promitto
